strict.criterion: Geographically distributed work groups collaborating online become a mainstream organizational norm rather than a niche enterprise tool.
strict.rationale: Cisco's 2007 WebEx acquisition noted 2.2 million registered accounts—a small fraction of global office workers—and physical co-location remained standard in 2009. Distributed remote and hybrid work groups became genuinely mainstream across organizations by 2019–2020 (Microsoft Teams alone reached 13 million daily active users in mid-2019 before surging in 2020).
changedConditions: Requires mainstream organizational adoption rather than an early 2.2M-account enterprise trend

reference.criterion: A strong practical trend toward geographically distributed collaboration emerges.
reference.rationale: Cisco’s 2007 WebEx acquisition described more than 2.2 million registered users collaborating online. Teams’ 2019 usage further substantiates the direction. The forecast does not require most workers to work remotely or the end of offices.
